body:
## Purpose

After the variance PR #4905, the dry convective boundary layer (Soares) has a liquid spike at its capping inversion. This arises because now we are sampling continuously, from the far tail of the SGS PDFs, leading to sampling of air cooler and moister than any actually available in the column. This is not realistic. Variances are generated by turbulent displacements, and they are finite. The relatively simple fix here is to cap the SGS distributions at some multiple of the standard deviation, with a new tuning parameter.

## Diagnosis

Since #4905 the equilibrium condensate is the full Gaussian expectation `E[max(0, S)]`, which is positive wherever `σ_S > 0`, however subsaturated the mean. In Soares, the capping inversion is about one cell thick: the `q_t` gradient across it is 1–2.2 g/kg per 100 m, against ≈ 0.5 g/kg per 100 m in PyCLES. The displacement (`ℓ_v ≈ 84 m`, about 1.7 Δz) acting on that gradient makes `σ_q` cycle between 0.2 and 1.0 g/kg as the inversion crosses cells; PyCLES `env_QTvar` gives 0.23–0.35 g/kg. (The 5–8 h mean is only ≈ 1.3× the LES, and the mixed-layer variances are 3–4× too small.) On the `σ_q` peaks, we get condensate spikes where `μ_S ≈ −3.6 σ_S`.

## Content

- `truncated_displacement_condensate(μ_S, σ_S, c)`: `E[max(0, S)]` for `S = μ_S + s σ_S x`, with the displacement `x` standard normal truncated to `[−c, c]` and stretched by `s = (1 − 2cφ(c)/Z)^(−1/2)`, `Z = Φ(c) − Φ(−c)`, so the variance of the covariance closure is unchanged. Closed form; zero for `μ_S ≤ −s c σ_S`; `c = Inf` returns `truncated_gaussian_condensate` bit for bit.
- `equilibrium_condensate(μ_S, σ_S, lin, curv, c)` selects it, or the curvature-aware `displacement_condensate` where `curv ≠ 0`, which is unchanged. It is used for the 1M equilibrium multiplier `λ_eq`, the 0M SGS saturation adjustment, and the variance fidelity.
- 1M: `λ_eq` is the mean of the Gaussian whose expectation is the truncated `q_c,eq` (`_continuous_lagrange`). Where `q_c,eq` vanishes, `λ_eq = −Inf` puts the equilibrium cloud edge at infinity, which the conditional-moment node rule gives zero weight. For `c = Inf`, `λ_eq = μ_S,cloud` as on `main`.
- New provisional parameter `sgs_displacement_truncation` (`c`, default 3, must be positive).

## Choice of `c`

Share of the Gaussian equilibrium condensate removed, evaluated offline on states recorded from the SCM runs:

| c | Soares | BOMEX | TRMM | RICO | DYCOMS RF01/RF02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.5 | 100 % | 3.1 % | 2.8 % | 0.4 % | ≈ 0 |
| 3 | 100 % | 1.3 % | 1.1 % | 0.07 % | ≈ 0 |
| 3.5 | 100 % | 0.4 % | 0.3 % | ≈ 0 | ≈ 0 |
| 4 | 60 % | 0.1 % | 0.1 % | ≈ 0 | ≈ 0 |

The least negative spike is at `μ_S/σ_S = −3.58`, so `c` must stay below about 3.5; `c = 3` (`s c ≈ 3.04`) leaves a margin. Almost all moist-case condensate comes from within three standard deviations.

## Verification

SCM runs of this branch against `main` (04d64029b), with the prognostic-EDMF 1M column configs:

| Case | LWP (fix vs main) | RWP | q_c,eq removed online |
|---|---|---|---|
| Soares | 0 (main: up to 9.4e-4 g/m²) | 0 | 100 % |
| BOMEX (t > 1 h) | +3.3 % | −4.3 % | 0.3 % |
| RICO (t > 2 h) | +0.4 % | +2.0 % | ≈ 0 |
| TRMM | −0.2 % | 0.0 % | 0.3 % |
| DYCOMS RF01 / RF02 (t > 1 h) | 0.0 % / +0.1 % | −0.1 % / 0.0 % | ≈ 0 |

GABLS has no condensate in either run. Before the rebase, a time-step perturbation of `main` (dt = 115 s instead of 120 s) changed BOMEX LWP by 6.5 %, RICO by 12 % and TRMM RWP by 22 %, so the differences above are within run-to-run spread.
title: Truncate the SGS displacement in the equilibrium condensate
